title: 181 more United ISD teachers earn state incentive pay — $5 million-plus headed to classrooms
excerpt: United ISD says 181 teachers earned a new or higher Teacher Incentive Allotment designation, bringing the district total to 328 and generating more than $5 million in teacher pay.
content:
United ISD is putting more money behind its best teachers. A total of 181 teachers received a new or higher Teacher Incentive Allotment designation, bringing the district's total to 328 designated teachers and generating more than $5 million in teacher compensation, according to United ISD.

The Texas Education Agency validated the district's Teacher Incentive Allotment results, confirming the 2024-2025 data and approving the 2025-2026 teacher designations. District leaders celebrated the news during a leadership training session, the district said.

Superintendent Dr. Gerardo Cruz said the designations let the district recognize excellence and retain it, keeping highly effective teachers in front of students. "This allows us not only to recognize excellence, but retain it, as we keep highly effective teachers in front of students where they are making a big impact," he said.

Teacher Incentive Allotment Director Vania Magallanes said the district submitted 487 teachers for designation and every one was approved. "We collect data from the beginning to the end of the year, measuring student performance growth and teacher observations," she said.

At Raul Perales Middle School, the impact was especially meaningful: the campus grew from four designated teachers last year to 14 this year. Principal Pamela Arredondo said the campus serves many economically disadvantaged and at-risk students, and that it takes dedication to get students to stay for tutorials and show academic growth.

The Teacher Incentive Allotment, created by the Texas Legislature, rewards highly effective teachers based on measurable student growth and instructional performance, with Recognized, Exemplary and Master designations. Dr. Cruz said the district's goal next year is to double the impact, with projections exceeding $11 million.

Source: United Independent School District (uisd.net).
